questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available where very important to me, as well as an exciting location.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy – I did sometimes struggle with the University's webpage, as you could be sent around through a million links before you find the necessary information, but you always find the information, you needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a few lectures and tours for visiting law students, which were quite helpful. We did not have a full week of introductory stuff though, you mostly had to seek out events and information yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard. I spent a few weeks on Spareroom, messaging anyone who had an open room. After a few weeks of working hard, it finally paid off. I would recommend being consistent and using sites like Spareroom, if you want to find something! I did not have a lot of luck with Facebook groups, most people would either try to scam you or just not reply.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is often not as social or fun as living in student housing, as your roommates will most likely be doing their own things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was quite disappointed with the student housing proces. I tried to get housing through the University, but they would not guarantee me anything for the longest time. I heard from them two weeks before we were supposed to start and was only offered something 45 minutes away from campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You would send a form with priorities for your courses and then a student advisor would try to get you those courses. You would hear back a few days after to see if you were able to get any of them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were very good as sending emails and guides on how to do this.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very hard to get the classes I wanted. I had a clear picture of what classes I wanted, but most of them were already full or they would have a policy, where they would only accept 2 visiting students or something like that. I was able (after a tough battle of sending many new course requests) to get 2/3 courses I wanted, so it turned out alright.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be persistent and keep trying to change your courses! They will do their best to listen and help out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was mostly in 3/4th year classes but also had a class that was both BA and MA students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Fairly different – I only had 3 two-hour seminars a week and the teaching style varied greatly. One teacher would do it more lecture-style, another focused on group discussions and another had more class-wide discussions. We did not really do any presentations or cases.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human Rights Honours
Business and Human Rights
Global Legal History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them, as I quite enjoyed them. I was able to learn something new in all of them, but also felt I had the relevant background knowledge.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any really. I think I spent most money on social activities, such as going out with friends to a pub, which can become quite expensive, when you do it quite often.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were mostly cheaper than at home. Other stuff such as coffee and food was quite expensive, just like home. Also, if you are over 22, you need to pay full bus prices, which always amounts to 2 pounds per trip.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many clubs and activities. They had a gym, sports classes, different societies (language societies, hobby societies, social societies) and also exchange student specific societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on some of the Erasmus Student Network trips to see some of Scotland! I also think the gym was very good, and would also just recommend joining different societies of your interests. I joined the yoga society, knit and crochet society, dance society and Scandinavian society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend exploring as much as Edinburgh as possible, but also trying to see more parts of Scotland. I went on hikes in the Highlands and small trips, such as to Glasgow.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, I don't think the culture was too different from the one at home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: From my experience, you are mostly introduced to other visiting students or international students, both through social events and your classes. I think most local students I met were freshman in the first week (who were all 18) or a few people in my classes, hence I did not engage with them a lot.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any differences very challenging, the Scottish dialect could be hard to understand sometimes though.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think the Scottish culture is so rich, full of so many traditions and so much history. I mostly loved the kindness of the Scotsmen – they were always very easy and nice to talk to! I also loved the pub-culture and the live music culture, as you could often find traditional Scottish music nights in the bars and clubs.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to all the events in the first week, make friends with as many people as possible and explore the beautiful surroundings.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think the University is very good at providing it, so be calm that you have it under control, they will always let you know about an upcoming deadline etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and the wonderful memories we had together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably the last two weeks of writing final exams, that was tough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
